Farmer–Citizen Movement: Netherlands. The Farmer–Citizen Movement (Dutch: BoerBurgerBeweging [buːrˈbʏrɣərbəˌʋeːɣɪŋ]; BBB) is an agrarian and right-wing populist political party in the Netherlands.

Radical Civic Union: Argentina. The Radical Civic Union (Spanish: Unión Cívica Radical, UCR) is a major political party in Argentina.
In which country is Battle of Königgrätz?
Battle of Königgrätz: Austria–Hungary. It took place on 3 July 1866, near the Bohemian city of Hradec Králové (German: Königgrätz) and village of Sadová, now in the Czech Republic.
In which country is Juche based?
Juche: North Korea. Juche, officially the Juche idea, is a name of the official ideology of North Korea and its ruling Workers' Party of Korea (WPK).

1995 Hanshin earthquake: Japan. It measured 6.9 on the moment magnitude scale and had a maximum intensity of 7 on the JMA Seismic Intensity Scale (XI–XII on the Modified Mercalli intensity scale).

Manchester Arena bombing: United Kingdom. On 22 May 2017, twenty-two people were killed and 1,017 injured in an Islamic terrorist suicide bombing at Manchester Arena in Manchester, England.

Rif War: Spanish protectorate in Morocco. The military operations in Jebala, in the Moroccan west, began in 1911 with the Larache landing.

Hyderabad State: Urdu. The state was ruled from 1724 to 1948 by the Nizam, who was initially a viceroy of the Mughal Empire in the Deccan.

Yugoslavia: Serbo-Croatian. Yugoslavia (lit. 'Land of the South Slavs') was a country in Central Europe and the Balkans that existed from 1918 to 1992.
Who is credited with discovering Big Bang?
Big Bang: Georges Lemaître. The Big Bang is a physical theory that describes how the universe expanded from an initial state of high density and temperature.
Succeeding Sani Abacha upon his death, this Nigerian general steered the country to multiparty elections and handed power to Olusegun Obasanjo in 1999 — who was he?
Abdulsalami Abubakar (born 13 June 1942) is a retired Nigerian army general who served as the military head of state of Nigeria from 1998 to 1999.

This Russian politician served as personal bodyguard to President Putin before rising to lead special forces that oversaw the 2014 annexation of Crimea, later becoming Deputy Defense Minister — who is he?
Aleksey Dyumin (born 28 August 1972) is a Russian politician serving as Secretary of the State Council since 2024.

Before he ever entered Parliament, this Welshman was a miners' union firebrand in the 1926 general strike — but he's best remembered for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service as Attlee's Minister of Health. Who was he?

Aneurin Bevan (15 November 1897 - 6 July 1960) was a Welsh Labour Party politician, noted for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service during his tenure as Minister of Health in Clement Attlee's government.

This Burmese politician and diplomat served as State Counsellor from 2016 to 2021 and was instrumental in Myanmar's transition from military rule toward democracy. She's been the general secretary of the National League for Democracy since the party's founding in 1988 — who is she?
Aung San Suu Kyi (born 19 June 1945) is a Burmese politician, diplomat and author who served as State Counsellor of Myanmar and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2016 to 2021.
Once Lord Mayor of Dublin, this Fianna Fáil leader became the second-longest-serving Taoiseach before resigning in 2008 amid the Mahon Tribunal's revelations — who is he?
Bertie Ahern (born 12 September 1951) is an Irish former Fianna Fil politician who served as Taoiseach from 1997 to 2008, and as Leader of Fianna Fil from 1994 to 2008.

Born to a Syrian family and raised Muslim, this Argentine president converted to Catholicism to pursue politics and ran the country for a full decade under his namesake brand of Peronism — who was he?
Carlos Menem (Spanish; 2 July 1930 - 14 February 2021) was an Argentine politician who served as the president of Argentina for ten years, from 1989 to 1999.

Nominated by President George H. W. Bush in 1991 to succeed Thurgood Marshall, this associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court is the second African American to serve on the bench and the second longest-serving justice in history. Who is he?
Clarence Thomas (born June 23, 1948) is an American lawyer and jurist who has served since 1991 as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
This category of evil supernatural being, believed in since possibly the Paleolithic age, appears across folklore, religion, and occultism worldwide — name it?
Demon is an evil or malevolent supernatural entity.
Widowed in 1945, this longest-serving American first lady reinvented her role and championed the text of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights at the UN — who was she?
Eleanor Roosevelt (October 11, 1884 - November 7, 1962) was an American political figure, diplomat, and activist.

Ferdinand Schörner (12 June 1892 - 2 July 1973) was a German military commander and convicted war criminal, who held the rank of Generalfeldmarschall (Field Marshal) in the Wehrmacht of Nazi Germany during World War II.
Which American politician, a convicted felon, served less than a year representing New York's 3rd district before being expelled from Congress in 2023?
George Santos (born July 22, 1988) is an American former politician and convicted felon.

Born to a farming family, this Indian politician served as chief minister of Karnataka before a roughly 11-month stint as prime minister of India in 1996-97, and has led his regional party since 1999. Who is he?
H. D. Deve Gowda (born 18 May 1933) is an Indian politician who served as the prime minister of India for nearly 11 months, from 1996 to 1997.
A leader of the army's 'Control Faction' in the 1930s, this officer became Japan's wartime prime minister in 1941; his rule was marked by widespread state violence — who is he?
Hideki Tojo (30 December 1884 - 23 December 1948) was a Japanese military officer and politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 1941 to 1944 during World War II.
Once rated Ukraine's second-richest man, this Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire co-founded PrivatBank in 1992 and later served as a regional governor during the early war with Russia — who is he?
Ihor Kolomoyskyi (born 13 February 1963) is a Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire businessman, once considered the leading oligarch in Ukraine.
Sent to take refuge on the Bass Rock as a boy after his escort was attacked, this youngest son of Robert III ruled the Scots from 1406 to 1437 — who was he?
James I of Scotland (late July 1394 - 21 February 1437) was King of Scots from 1406 to 1437.

Born in Centreville, Mississippi and educated at Vanderbilt, UVA Law, and Oxford, this Republican has served as Louisiana's junior U.S. Senator since 2017 after 17 years as the state's Treasurer — name this politician?
John Kennedy (Louisiana politician) (born November 21, 1951) is an American politician and attorney who has served as the junior United States senator from Louisiana since 2017.
A WWI U-boat commander taken prisoner by the British in 1918, he later briefly became Nazi Germany's head of state after Hitler's suicide — who is it?

Karl Dönitz (16 September 1891 - 24 December 1980) was a German naval officer and politician who briefly succeeded Adolf Hitler as the head of state of Nazi Germany after the latter's suicide during the World War II in April 1945.
Widow of warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi, this Buddhist nun founded a temple in Kyoto and monitored daimyo families held hostage at Osaka Castle — who was she?
Kōdai-in (died October 17, 1624), formerly known as Nene, One, Nei, was an aristocrat and Buddhist nun, founder of the temple Kdai-ji in Kyoto, Japan.
A Spanish Navy officer who fought in the Rif War and Civil War before rising through Franco's government, he was handpicked as the dictator's successor as head of government — who is he?
Luis Carrero Blanco (Spanish; 4 March 1904 - 20 December 1973) was a Spanish Navy officer and politician.
This retired U.S. Army general served as the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2019 to 2023, after earlier serving as the Army's 39th chief of staff — who is he?
Mark Milley (born 20 June 1958) is a retired United States Army general who served as the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2019 to 2023.
She served as deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland from 2020 to 2022 before rising to First Minister in 2024 — who is she?
Michelle O'Neill (ne Doris; born 10 January 1977) is an Irish politician who has been First Minister of Northern Ireland since February 2024 and Vice President of Sinn Fin since 2018.
This former footballer and journalist represented the Heingang constituency and rose to become Manipur's 12th Chief Minister, serving from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?

N. Biren Singh (Meitei; born 1 January 1961) is an Indian politician, former footballer and journalist who served as the 12th Chief Minister of Manipur from 2017 to 2025 as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
This Indian politician has served as Minister of Road Transport & Highways since 2014, becoming the only person to hold that single portfolio for three consecutive terms — who is he?
Nitin Gadkari (born 27 May 1957) is an Indian politician who is serving as the 40th Minister of Road Transport & Highways since 2014.
Also known for the character Professor Kranz, this Italian actor and writer penned satirical books and became famous for grotesque comic creations, including a meek accountant — who is he?
Paolo Villaggio (30 December 1932 - 3 July 2017) was an Italian actor, comedian, film director, and writer.
Whether offered alone or in groups, as part of a set ritual or spontaneously, this act of communication with a deity can seek intercession, give thanks, or offer praise — what is it called?
Prayer is an invocation or act that seeks to activate a rapport with an object of worship through deliberate communication.
After leading the Congress to victory in the 2023 state election that toppled the incumbent Bharat Rashtra Samithi, which politician became the current Chief Minister of Telangana?
Revanth Reddy (born 8 November 1969) is an Indian politician who is serving as the second and current Chief Minister of Telangana.
Born in London to a Pakistani family and once a practicing solicitor, this Labour politician represented Tooting in Parliament before becoming the city's mayor in 2016 — who is he?
Sadiq Khan (born 8 October 1970) is a British politician serving as the third and current strategic authority mayor for London since 2016.
Known by the honorific 'Bangabandhu,' this Bengali politician led his country to independence and served as its founding president before being assassinated in a 1975 coup — who is he?

Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (17 March 1920 - 15 August 1975), also known as Mujib or by the honorific Bangabandhu, was a Bangladeshi politician, revolutionary, statesman, activist and diarist who was the founding president of Bangladesh.
Once a mere province under the Bahmani Kingdom, it broke free in 1490 to become one of the Deccan's most powerful states — until Aurangzeb's Mughals swallowed it in 1686. What kingdom was it?
Sultanate of Bijapur was an early modern kingdom in the western Deccan and South India, ruled by the Muslim Adil Shahi (or Adilshahi) dynasty.

Elected king by Ostrogothic nobles in 541 after his two predecessors were murdered for trying to surrender, this skilled commander reversed the tide of the Gothic War and clawed back nearly all of Italy by 543. Who is he?
Totila (died 1 July 552), was the penultimate King of the Ostrogoths, reigning from 541 to 552.
This Russian right-wing populist politician led a nationalist party from its 1992 founding until his death in 2022, twice serving as deputy chairman of the State Duma. Who is he?

Vladimir Zhirinovsky (25 April 1946 - 6 April 2022) was a Russian right-wing populist politician who served as the leader of the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR) from its creation in 1992 until his death in 2022.
Born in Virginia and holding a Ph.D. from Johns Hopkins, this 28th president led the nation through World War I and lent his name to a foreign-policy doctrine — who was he?
Woodrow Wilson (December 28, 1856 - February 3, 1924) was the 28th president of the United States, serving from 1913 to 1921.
Touched off when Hezbollah ambushed Israeli soldiers on the border in July 2006, this 34-day conflict ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire — what is it called?
2006 Lebanon War: Armed conflict primarily between Israel and Hezbollah.
Castrated as a child by a rival's successor, he nonetheless reunified Iran, made Tehran the capital, and founded a dynasty as its first Shah. Who was he?
Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar: Shah of Iran from 1789 to 1797.

Alexander Kolchak: Russian admiral and White movement leader (1874–1920)

António Costa: President of the European Council since 2024. António Luís Santos da Costa (born 17 July 1961) is a Portuguese lawyer and politician who has served as president of the European Council since 2024.
A close ally of President Macron, this French politician has served as Minister for Equality between Women and Men and previously as Minister for Solidarity and Family — who is she?
Aurore Bergé: French politician and Minister. Previously, Bergé represented the 10th constituency of the Yvelines department in the National Assembly since 2017.

The longest continuous military campaign of World War II, this naval struggle pitted German U-boats against Allied convoys ferrying supplies from North America to Britain and the Soviet Union — what's this campaign called?
Battle of the Atlantic: Attempt by Germany during World War II to cut supply lines to Britain.

Blogger (service): American online content management system.

Canaan Banana: President of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 1987.

A fighter pilot with over 3,000 flight hours, this retired Air Force general became the first African American to lead a branch of the US Armed Forces and served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2023 to 2025 — who is he?
Charles Q. Brown Jr.: US Air Force general (born 1962)
The half-sister of Helen of Troy and wife of Mycenae's king, this figure from Greek mythology murdered her husband upon his return from Troy to avenge the sacrifice of their daughter — who is she?
Clytemnestra: Figure from Greek mythology. Clytemnestra appears as a character in several ancient Greek works, including the Homeric epics and plays by Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides.
Serving as the 44th vice president under George H. W. Bush, this Republican represented Indiana in both the House and Senate before his time in the White House — who is he?
Dan Quayle: Vice President of the United States from 1989 to 1993.

Meaning 'the owner of two horns,' this Quranic figure travels east and west and builds a barrier to hold back Gog and Magog. Most historians link the story to legends about a famous ancient conqueror. Who is he?
Dhu'l-Qarnayn: Figure in the Quran. Dhu'l-Qarnayn has most popularly been identified by Western and traditional Muslim scholars as Alexander the Great.
The sixth person to walk on the Moon spent nine hours in the Fra Mauro Highlands as Apollo 14's Lunar Module Pilot, and later became a noted ufologist — who was he?
Edgar Mitchell: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1930–2016)

Emmerson Mnangagwa: President of Zimbabwe since 2017. Mnangagwa was re-elected in the 2023 Zimbabwean general election with 52.6% of the vote.
After a 53-day siege in 1453, Sultan Mehmed II captured the Byzantine capital and made it the new Ottoman seat of power — which watershed event is this?
Fall of Constantinople: 1453 Ottoman conquest of the Byzantine capital. The city was captured on 29 May 1453 as part of the culmination of a 53-day siege which had begun on 6 April.
Regarded as one of history's most brutal dictators, this man led Equatorial Guinea to independence in 1968 before his erratic, cult-of-personality rule ended in a 1979 overthrow — who was he?
Francisco Macías Nguema: President of Equatorial Guinea from 1968 to 1979.
Convicted of murdering 49 women in the Pacific Northwest, this killer was nicknamed for the Washington river where his first five victims were found — who was he?

A leader of the First Crusade, this nobleman became the first ruler of a newly captured holy city in 1099 but declined the title of king, choosing 'Advocate of the Holy Sepulchre' instead — who is he?
Godfrey of Bouillon: Ruler of Jerusalem from 1099 to 1100.
A key player in the 1963 Ba'athist coup, this Syrian officer ruled as president from 1971 until his death in 2000 — and passed power to his son. Who was he?

Hafez al-Assad: President of Syria from 1971 to 2000. Hafez al-Assad (6 October 1930 – 10 June 2000) was a Syrian politician and military officer who served as the president of Syria from 1971 until his death in 2000.
A German general and military theorist, he pioneered the 'blitzkrieg' approach and was central to developing the panzer division concept and tank warfare — who was he?
Heinz Guderian: German Wehrmacht Heer general (1888–1954)
Founded in Jordanian-controlled Jerusalem in 1953 by a Palestinian religious-court judge, this pan-Islamist group seeks to reestablish a global caliphate under sharia — which organization?

Hizb ut-Tahrir: Pan-Islamist and fundamentalist organization. The organization sees world history as an eternal conflict between Islam and non-believers, with the state system considered a historical assault on Islam.

This fighter pilot turned prime minister was the first Rhodesian leader born and raised in the country, and led the white government that unilaterally declared independence from Britain in 1965. Who was he?
Ian Smith: Prime Minister of Rhodesia from 1964 to 1979.

Inheriting leadership of a Sufi military order from his brother as a child, this ruler founded a Persian dynasty in 1501 and unified Iran under native rule for the first time in over eight centuries. Who was he?
Ismail I: Shah of Safavid Iran from 1501 to 1524.
Representing Maryland's 8th congressional district since 2017, this progressive Democrat also founded Democracy Summer, a nationwide youth civic-organizing program — who is he?
A scholar and lawyer who inherited the Trujillo era's secretive, caudillo style, he served three non-consecutive terms as president of the Dominican Republic between 1960 and 1996 — who was he?
Joaquín Balaguer: President of the Dominican Republic (1960–1961, 1966–1978, 1986–1996)
Born in Georgia and rising as a Soviet revolutionary, this figure led from 1924 to 1953 while consolidating power into a dictatorship and codifying Marxism–Leninism — who was he?
Joseph Stalin: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1953.
A German naval officer who once commanded U-boat UB-68 in WWI, he briefly became Nazi Germany's head of state after Hitler's suicide in April 1945 — who is it?

Ruled for most of its existence by Regent Miklos Horthy despite having no actual monarch on the throne, this interwar Central European state emerged after the suppression of a short-lived Soviet republic during the White Terror — which nation?
Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1946): Monarchy under regency.
An ethnic Georgian who rose through the Cheka and became head of the NKVD in 1938, this secret police chief organized the Katyn massacre and ended his predecessor Yezhov's purge — who is he?
Lavrentiy Beria: Soviet secret police chief (1899–1953)
Affectionately nicknamed 'Nessie,' this long-necked cryptid supposedly lurking in a Scottish Highlands lake shot to worldwide fame in 1933 — what is it?
Loch Ness Monster: Mythical creature in Scottish folklore.
Elected in 2020, this North Carolina congressman became the first member of Congress born in the 1990s, before controversies helped end his reelection bid in 2022 — who is he?
Twice queen consort of England through her marriage to Henry the Sixth, this daughter of the King of Naples personally led the Lancastrian side during the Wars of the Roses — who is she?
Margaret of Anjou: Queen of England (1445–1461, 1470–1471)
A brigadier general who led El Salvador through most of World War II, he served as the country's 27th president until resigning in 1944 — which Salvadoran officer?
Maximiliano Hernández Martínez: President of El Salvador from 1931 to 1934 and 1935 to 1944.
Plucked from running Russia's Federal Taxation Service, this economist was confirmed as prime minister in a single day in January 2020 after the entire previous government resigned — who is it?
Mikhail Mishustin: Russian politician and economist (born 1966)
Hidden by his mother among the bulrushes of the Nile as a baby, this prophet grew up to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt. Who is he?
More than just nudism, this lifestyle and movement frames non-sexual social nudity around harmony with nature and respect for the environment — what is it called?
Naturism: Practice and advocacy of social nudity.

Sparked by a 1962 coup that toppled a newly crowned king and proclaimed a republic — and even abolished slavery — this conflict pitted royalists backed near the Saudi border against the new government. Which war was it?
North Yemen civil war: 1962–1970 conflict. The war began with a coup d'état carried out in 1962 by revolutionary republicans led by the army under the command of Abdullah al-Sallal.
Hebrew for 'Jewish Power,' this far-right Israeli political party grew out of the banned Kach movement and was linked in its early years to politician Itamar Ben-Gvir — which party?
Otzma Yehudit: Israeli far-right political party. Otzma ran independently in the 2013 election and as part of a list with ultra-Orthodox party Yachad in 2015.
Based on the doctrine of a 20th-century Argentine leader, this political movement is defined by three 'flags' — social justice, economic independence, and political sovereignty — what is it called?
Peronism: Argentine political movement. Peronism, also known as justicialism, is an Argentine ideology and political movement, based on the ideas, doctrine, and legacy of Juan Perón (1895–1974).
This act of deliberate communication with a deity — through hymns, incantations, or spontaneous words — has been documented in written sources for some five thousand years — what is it called?
Prayer: Invocation or act that seeks to activate a rapport with a deity.
Ascending the Siamese throne in 1782 following the deposition of King Taksin, this monarch became the first ruler of the Chakri dynasty and founded the city that is now Bangkok — who was he?
Rama I: King of Siam from 1782 to 1809.
A Labour politician who served two decades on the Kensington and Chelsea council, she also worked as a senior lecturer at Kingston University — who is she?
Rima Horton: English former councillor and economics lecturer (born 1947)
Beginning on 24 February 2022, this conflict became the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II and sparked the continent's biggest refugee crisis in that span — what is it?
Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present): Phase since 2022 of war ongoing since 2014.
The daughter of a former Arkansas governor, this politician became the third woman ever to serve as White House press secretary before winning the Arkansas governorship herself in 2022 — who is she?
Sarah Huckabee Sanders: Governor of Arkansas since 2023.
At just 13 he became the youngest sole emperor of the united Roman Empire, succeeding his slain cousin Elagabalus as the last ruler of the Severan dynasty. Who was he?
Severus Alexander: Roman emperor from 222 to 235.
Founded in 1905 by Arthur Griffith, this Irish party's members established the revolutionary First Dáil and fought in the War of Independence — which party?
Sinn Féin: Political party in Ireland.
A British barrister who twice held the post of Home Secretary in 2022, this MP for Fareham made headlines in January 2026 by defecting from the Conservatives to Reform UK — who is she?
The son of Odysseus and Penelope, this young man sailed to Pylos and Sparta seeking news of his father, then helped slay the suitors back home in Ithaca — who is he?
Telemachus: Mythological son of Odysseus. When Telemachus reached manhood, he visited Pylos and Sparta in search of his wandering father.

The United Nations was established by the signing of the Charter of the United Nations on 26 June 1945, with the mission of maintaining international peace and security.

Vladimir Lenin: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1924.
Crowned King of Prussia in 1861, this Hohenzollern monarch became the first emperor of a unified Germany a decade later — who was he?
Wilhelm I: German Emperor from 1871 to 1888.
Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams to promote 'muscular Christianity,' this youth organization now serves over 64 million people worldwide?
YMCA: Worldwide youth organization. YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.
Founder of the Pakistan People's Party, this barrister-statesman served as both president and prime minister of Pakistan before his 1977 overthrow and 1979 execution — who was he?
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto: 4th President and 9th Prime Minister of Pakistan (1928–1979)
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Franz Reichelt (born 1878) is the earliest of the four. The parachute failed to deploy and he plummeted 57 metres (187 ft) to his death.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
TeX (published 1978) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow is a physicist.
Which one below is best known as a chemist?
Willard Libby is a chemist. For his contributions to the team that developed this process, Libby was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1960.
What is the atomic number of Fluorine?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
In what year was Hedy Lamarr born?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 – January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.
In what year was Acupuncture discovered?
Acupuncture is a form of alternative medicine and a component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which thin needles are inserted into the body.
In what year was SARS-CoV-2 discovered?
SARS-CoV-2: The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
Furosemide: Pfizer. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
In which country is Māori language?
Māori language: New Zealand. The southernmost member of the Austronesian language family, it is related to Cook Islands Māori, Tuamotuan, and Tahitian.
Who is credited with discovering Infrared?
Infrared: William Herschel. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Who is credited with discovering Cherenkov radiation?
Cherenkov radiation: Sergey Vavilov. A classic example of Cherenkov radiation is the characteristic blue glow of an underwater nuclear reactor.
Who is credited with discovering Argon?
Argon: William Ramsay. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Made of adenine bonded to a sugar, this RNA building block underlies ATP, the cell's main energy currency, and doubles as an IV treatment for certain cardiac arrhythmias — what is it?
Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
This white crystalline chemical compound is mainly used as a high-nitrogen agricultural fertilizer, but is also a key ingredient in explosive mixtures used for mining and quarrying — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate is a chemical compound with the formula NH4NO3.
The 16th-largest family of flowering plants, this aromatic group includes cumin, fennel, and coriander alongside deadly relatives like water hemlock — which family?
Apiaceae is a family of mostly aromatic flowering plants named after the type genus Apium, and commonly known as the celery, carrot, or parsley family, or simply as umbellifers.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.
This brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal can develop a vividly iridescent, rainbow-colored surface from thin-film oxidation when heated. What element is it?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
One of only two elements liquid at room temperature, this reddish-brown, pungent-smelling element takes its name from the Greek word for 'stench.' What element is it (symbol Br)?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
Along with the bonobo, which great ape of equatorial Africa's forests and savannas is humans' closest living relative, according to DNA and fossil evidence?
Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.

Making up 25 to 35 percent of protein content in mammals, this triple-helix structural protein is the main component of the extracellular matrix in cartilage, bone, tendons, and skin — name the protein?
Collagen is the main structural protein in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues of many animals.
This breaded, deep-fried snack binds a thick sauce like béchamel with fillings such as meat, seafood, or cheese, and was originally a way to use up leftovers — what is it?
Croquette is a deep-fried roll originating in French cuisine and most extended in Spanish cuisine consisting of a thick binder combined with a filling, which is then breaded.
Mother of Princess Alia, this royal later remarried a senior PLO official in 1970 after her short-lived marriage to Jordan's king ended — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid (15 December 1929 - 21 August 2019) was a Hashemite princess and Queen of Jordan from 1955 until 1957 as the first wife of King Hussein.
Discovered to have two undescribed relatives only in 2019, this Amazonian 'knifefish' is best known for generating powerful electric discharges — which species?
Electrophorus electricus is the best-known species of electric eel. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
Aerobic exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all induce this intense feeling of well-being — which is also, less happily, a symptom of mania — what state is it?
Euphoria (yoo-) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
Madagascar's largest carnivore, this slender, long-tailed mammal evolved cougar-like features independently and climbs trees head-first thanks to flexible ankles — what is it?
Fossa (animal) (Cryptoprocta ferox; FOSS- or) is a slender, long-tailed, cat-like mammal that is endemic to Madagascar.
This flowering plant genus, whose name derives from the Latin word for a small sword, belongs to the iris family and is centered on the Cape Floristic Region of South Africa — which genus?
Gladiolus (from Latin, the diminutive of gladius, a sword) is a genus of perennial cormous flowering plants in the iris family (Iridaceae).
These seed-loving rodents come in 19 species, the golden or Syrian variety being the one most often found in a child's bedroom cage — what are they?
Hamster are rodents (order Rodentia) belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae, which contains 19 species classified in seven genera.

Despite resembling a common shellfish, this ancient arthropod is actually a chelicerate more closely related to spiders and scorpions, and is often called a 'living fossil' for its unchanged ancient body plan — what is it?
Horseshoe crab are arthropods of the family Limulidae and the only surviving xiphosurans.
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length is often understood as roughly the width of a human thumb — name the unit?
Inch (symbol: in or) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
This self-described 'constitutional law attorney' joined Trump's inner circle in November 2019, though reporters found she'd never argued a federal case — who is she?
Jenna Ellis (born November 1, 1984) is an American conservative suspended lawyer who was a member of Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign's legal team.

First described in 1845 by a German physicist, these two fundamental equalities govern how current and voltage behave in an electrical network, building on Georg Ohm's earlier work — what are they called?
Kirchhoff's circuit laws are two equalities that deal with the current and potential difference (commonly known as voltage) in the lumped element model of electrical circuits.
A Ming-dynasty naturalist poured 27 years into a sprawling pharmacology compendium of nearly 1,900 entries, 11,000 prescriptions, and over a thousand herbs — who was this herbalist and physician?
Li Shizhen (July 3, 1518 - 1593), courtesy name Dongbi, was a Chinese acupuncturist, herbalist, naturalist, pharmacologist, physician, and writer of the Ming dynasty.
About 90% of its cases fall into the non-Hodgkin variety, and its tell-tale signs include painless swollen lymph nodes and night sweats — which group of white-blood-cell cancers is this?
Lymphoma is a group of blood and lymph tumors that develop from lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell).

Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German theoretical physicist is considered the originator of quantum theory and one of the founders of modern physics — who is he?
Max Planck (23 April 1858 - 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
Widowed in 2021, this Israeli-American billionaire physician publishes Israel Hayom and has been among the most prominent financial supporters of a US president since 2016 — who is she?
Miriam Adelson (ne Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
Also called the coypu, this plant-eating rodent digs streamside burrows and now troubles several countries as an invasive species far from its South American home — what is it?
Nutria (Myocastor coypus) is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent from South America.

Covered in large protective keratin scales, these mammals — sometimes called scaly anteaters — range across Asia and sub-Saharan Africa and are the only mammal order known to have such scales — what are they?
Pangolin are mammals of the order Pholidota. The one extant family, the Manidae, has three genera: Manis, Phataginus, and Smutsia.
A self-described socialist active in Finland's Pirate Party, this entrepreneur co-founded a famous file-sharing search engine and later started the privacy service Njalla — who is he?
Peter Sunde (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
Emerging roughly 203 million years ago and wiped out alongside the dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this order of long-necked marine reptiles ruled Jurassic seas — what were they?
Plesiosaur are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
The only member of the genus Rangifer, this circumpolar deer of the Arctic tundra goes by another name entirely in North America — what is it?
Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.
A botanist active in Japan's Meiji era, this scholar died in 1899 after decades of scientific work — who was he?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (October 13, 1851 - August 8, 1899) was a Japanese botanist during the Meiji era.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Known in Hispanic America as guanábana and easily killed by a touch of frost, which Annona fruit blends flavors of strawberry, apple, and sour citrus?
Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanbana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
The only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands, found on the Indonesian island of Sumatra after its Bali and Javan cousins went extinct in the 20th century — what is it?
Sumatran tiger is a population of Panthera tigris sondaica on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.

Governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work and temperature to energy and entropy, this branch of physics underpins chemical, mechanical and biochemical engineering alike — which field of physics?
Thermodynamics is a branch of physics that deals with heat, work, and temperature, and their relation to energy, entropy, and the physical properties of matter and radiation.
Several highly prized truffle species belong to this fungal genus, whose lineage is estimated to date to the close of the Jurassic period — which genus?
Tuber (fungus) is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

Commanding the first spaceflight to carry multiple crew members in 1964, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first human to die during a space mission when his capsule's parachute failed on reentry in 1967 — who was he?
Vladimir Komarov (16 March 1927 - 24 April 1967) was a Soviet test pilot, aerospace engineer, and cosmonaut.

This Polish-American scholar served as Jimmy Carter's national security advisor from 1977 to 1981 and helped organize an influential international policy group known as the Trilateral Commission — who is he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski (March 28, 1928 - May 26, 2017) was a Polish-American diplomat and political scientist.
This term for cancer that begins in gland cells applies to the most common form of breast cancer and one of the two major types of esophageal cancer — which term?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma: Cancer of epithelial cells with glandular origin or characteristics.

Often called the greatest mathematician of the twentieth century, this German-born Frenchman revolutionized algebraic geometry before abruptly leaving his post at a Paris research institute in 1970 — who is he?
This memory disorder comes in two main forms — one blocking recall of events before a specific date, the other preventing new experiences from becoming lasting memories — what is it?
Amnesia: Cognitive disorder where memory is disturbed or lost.
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)
This order of even-toed hoofed mammals turns out to include whales and dolphins, molecular biology having revealed their close kinship to hippos — what order is it?
Artiodactyla: Order of mammals. Artiodactyla ( AR-tee-oh-DAK-tih-lə; from Ancient Greek ἄρτιος ártios 'even' and δάκτυλος dáktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.
Native to the steppes of Central Asia, this two-humped pack animal's cold and drought tolerance made it indispensable to Silk Road caravans — what is it?
Bactrian camel: Species of mammal of Asia.
Known as silver birch for its peeling white bark, this deciduous tree native to Europe and Asia has become invasive in parts of North America — which species?
Betula pendula: Species of birch. Its range extends into Siberia, China, and southwest Asia in the mountains of northern Turkey, the Caucasus, and northern Iran.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?
Present in the gut or mouth of up to 60 percent of healthy adults, this opportunistic yeast turns dangerous in immunocompromised patients, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans: Species of fungus. Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
Named after a Louisiana parish and named the state's official canine in 1979, this herding breed was traditionally used to hunt feral boars — what breed is it?
Catahoula Leopard Dog: American breed of dog.
Built after a 1962 tech-transfer deal with the Soviets fell short on documentation, this Chinese fighter jet is a reverse-engineered derivative of the MiG-21 — which aircraft?
Chengdu J-7: Chinese version of the Soviet MiG-21.
This lincosamide antibiotic treats infections from strep throat to acne, but raises the risk of a specific gut infection roughly fourfold — what is it?
Clindamycin: Antibiotic. It can also be used to treat acne, and some cases of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
Its species name honors Colchis, an ancient region on the Black Sea, and it's often released into the wild as a game bird — which Asian-native, ring-necked bird is this?
Common pheasant: Species of bird. The common pheasant (Phasianus colchicus), ring-necked pheasant, or blue-headed pheasant, is a bird in the pheasant family (Phasianidae).
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.
At just 37 this American biologist won a 1975 Nobel for discovering reverse transcriptase, later running Caltech and founding the Whitehead Institute — who is he?
David Baltimore: American biologist and Nobel laureate (1938–2025)
These warmblooded reptiles ruled the land for the whole Mesozoic, and one feathered lineage of theirs survived the extinction 66 million years ago as today's birds — what group is this?
Dinosaur: Clade of reptiles. Since then, mounted fossil dinosaur skeletons have been major attractions at museums worldwide, and dinosaurs have become an enduring part of popular culture.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.
Occurring in the cytosol, this ten-step metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate while generating ATP and NADH — what process is it?
Glycolysis: Series of interconnected biochemical reactions.
Also nicknamed the millionfish, this livebearing freshwater fish is one of the world's most popular aquarium species — which fish?

This airway symptom — blood or blood-streaked mucus coughed up from the lungs or throat — turns dangerous mainly because of choking rather than blood loss once it passes 300 milliliters. What is it called?
Damage to the sympathetic trunk nerves produces this trio of symptoms on one side of the face — a constricted pupil, a droopy eyelid, and reduced sweating — what is this condition called?
Horner's syndrome: Facial disorder due to damage of the sympathetic nerves.
This condition describes a shortage of oxygen at the tissue level rather than in the blood itself, and can occur normally during intense exercise — what is it?
Hypoxia (medicine): Medical condition of lack of oxygen in the tissues.

A functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel movement consistency over long periods, sometimes years, it can negatively affect quality of life and is associated with anxiety and depression. What condition is this?
Irritable bowel syndrome: Functional gastrointestinal disorder. The cause of IBS is not known but multiple factors have been proposed to lead to the condition.
This British chemical engineer founded a major chemicals group in 1998 and later became a minority shareholder with control over football operations at Manchester United — who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe: British engineer and businessman (born 1952)
Its subfamily name literally means 'large foot,' it's native to Australia and New Guinea, and a 2019 government tally counted some 42.8 million of them in harvest areas. Which marsupial?
Kangaroo: Marsupial of the family Macropodidae.
Also called the Mediterranean black widow, this venomous spider is common throughout the Mediterranean region and central Asia — what species is it?

Latrodectus tredecimguttatus: Species of spider. Latrodectus tredecimguttatus, also known as the Mediterranean black widow or the European black widow, is a species in the genus Latrodectus of the widow spiders.
Native to the Indo-Pacific, this venomous aquarium favorite sports red-and-black banded warning colors and ostentatious spiny fins, and has become an invasive nightmare in the Caribbean — what is it?
Named from the Latin for "wolf," this autoimmune disease often announces itself with a red facial rash and alternates between flares and remission — what is it?
Lupus: Autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
Boiled down from its sap to make a beloved breakfast syrup, this genus of roughly 132 tree and shrub species counts the sycamore as its type species — which genus of trees?
Nicknamed a 'semi-lunar' cartilage for its half-moon shape, this crescent-shaped structure cushions joints like the knee, wrist, and jaw — what is it?
Meniscus (anatomy): Fibrocartilaginous part of a bone joint.
Based on a Soviet fighter jet but optimized for ground attack, this variable-sweep aircraft was license-built in India as the 'Bahadur,' or 'Valiant' — which jet?
Mikoyan MiG-27: Series of 1970s Soviet attack aircraft.

First identified from skulls found in a Dutch chalk quarry near Maastricht and initially mistaken for crocodile or whale bones, this giant marine lizard genus lived until 66 million years ago — which genus is it?
Mosasaurus: Extinct genus of marine lizard from the Late Cretaceous.
Colloquially known as a moon, this type of astronomical body orbits a planet or dwarf planet, with 455 confirmed examples across the Solar System's six major systems — what is it called?
Natural satellite: Astronomical body that orbits a planet. Natural satellites are colloquially referred to as moons, by analogy with the Moon, Earth's natural satellite.
This American physicist won the 1989 Nobel for inventing the separated oscillatory field method behind atomic clocks, and helped found both Brookhaven National Laboratory and Fermilab — who was he?

Numbering 126 species, these are the largest order of marsupials in the Western Hemisphere — and only one of them, the Virginia variety, made it as far north as the United States and Canada. What animal is this?

Named after the bones that house them — frontal, maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid — these four paired air-filled spaces surround the nasal cavity and have a still-debated evolutionary purpose — what are they called?
Paranasal sinuses: Air-filled spaces surrounding the nasal cavity.
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
Scientifically named Cajanus cajan, this perennial Fabaceae legume is a staple crop across the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean — what is it?
Pigeon pea: Species of perennial legume. The pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.
Though they look like dolphins, these small toothed whales are actually closer kin to narwhals and belugas, with flat spade-shaped teeth instead of dolphins' cone-shaped ones — what are they called?
Porpoise: Small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae.
This holotropical bird family comprises a dozen Afrotropical species and some 167 Neotropical species, including the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which family is this?
Psittacidae: Family of birds. The family Psittacidae or holotropical parrots is one of three families of true parrots.
After his Jewish family fled Germany, this engineer at Sanders Associates dreamed up playing games on a TV screen and built a 'Brown Box' that became the first home video game console — who is he?
Ralph H. Baer: American inventor and engineer (1922–2014)
This English anatomist coined the word 'Dinosauria' — 'terrible reptile' — yet remained an outspoken critic of Darwin's theory of natural selection — who is it?
Richard Owen: English biologist and palaeontologist (1804–1892)

Formed by the fusion of five vertebrae between the ages of 18 and 30, this triangular bone sits at the base of the spine and connects to the tailbone below and the last lumbar vertebra above. What is it?
Sacrum: Bone of the spine. The sacrum situates at the upper, back part of the pelvic cavity, between the two wings of the pelvis.
Named from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster,' this small bony fish sports an upright posture, a curled tail, and bony armor plating — which creature is it?
Blurring the line between a single creature and a colony, this cnidarian is actually made of specialized zooids from one fertilized egg working together to float, feed and jet-propel — what is it?
Siphonophore: Order of colonial hydrozoans with differentiated zooids.
With over 60 types found throughout the human body, this ring-shaped muscle keeps a bodily passage closed until it relaxes to let something through — what is it called?
Sphincter: Circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice.
This colorless, sweet-smelling liquid made from benzene is the precursor to polystyrene, with global production reaching some 35 million tonnes by 2018 — what compound is it?
Styrene: Chemical compound. Styrene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H5CH=CH2.
One of the largest parasitoid wasps, this creature paralyzes its eight-legged prey with a sting, drags it into a nest, and lays a single egg so the larva can devour the still-living host. What is it?
Tarantula hawk: Common name for two genera of wasps.
Best known for his 1651 work 'Leviathan' and its influential take on social contract theory, this English philosopher once met Galileo while tutoring the Cavendish family across Europe — who was he?
Thomas Hobbes: English philosopher and political theorist (1588–1679)
Only about 76 to 90 nucleotides long, this adaptor molecule reads each three-letter mRNA codon with a matching anticodon and ferries the right amino acid to the ribosome — what is it?
Transfer RNA: RNA that facilitates the addition of amino acids to a new protein.
Element 121, this not-yet-synthesized superactinide is expected to open a brand-new g-block of the periodic table and may sit on the 'island of stability' — what's its placeholder name?
Unbiunium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 121 (Ubu)
Running a boutique called Sex with partner Malcolm McLaren, this English designer helped bring punk fashion into the mainstream and shaped the look of the Sex Pistols — who is she?
A short-legged, stubby-tailed marsupial native to Australia, this burrowing animal can weigh up to 35 kilograms and survives in an isolated pocket of central Queensland — which creature?
Wombat: Species of marsupial native to Australia.
Protactinium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for protactinium is Pa. Protactinium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pa and atomic number 91.
The symbol for polonium is Po. Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.

Alain Delon: Alain Fabien Maurice Marcel Delon (French: [alɛ̃ dəlɔ̃]; 8 November 1935 – 18 August 2024) was a French actor, film producer, screenwriter, singer, and businessman.
In what year was Steve McQueen born?
Steve McQueen: Terrence Stephen McQueen (March 24, 1930 – November 7, 1980) was an American actor.
